q: A traditional-method sparkler built on Macabeo, Xarel-lo and Parellada carries which name?
exp: Cava is defined by its method rather than by a single place, though the great majority comes from Penedes in Catalonia. Chardonnay and Pinot Noir are permitted alongside the three traditional grapes.

q: Growers work a ridge of Cretaceous chalk belonging to the same seam that lies beneath Champagne, and their traditional-method Chardonnay and Pinot Noir have drawn serious attention since the 1990s. Which region is this?
exp: The chalk of the North and South Downs and the chalk of the Marne belong to one Late Cretaceous formation, interrupted by the Channel. Warmer seasons are what finally let the fruit ripen at the acidity a sparkling base wants, and the plantings are dominated by the three Champagne varieties.

q: Lombardy's benchmark bottle-fermented sparkler, built largely on Chardonnay and Pinot Noir, is sold as what?
exp: Franciacorta uses the traditional method with long lees ageing. Its Saten style is an all-white blend bottled at lower pressure for a softer, creamier mousse.

q: At around five and a half percent alcohol and only gently fizzy, Moscato d'Asti gets its sweetness how?
opts: Spirit is added to halt the fermentation
A single ferment is chilled to a halt
The grapes are dried before pressing
Sugar is added just before bottling
exp: Chilling and filtering arrest the ferment in tank, so the wine keeps grape sugar, low alcohol and a pressure well short of a full spumante.

q: A German sparkling wine made entirely from the grower's own fruit is labelled how?
exp: Winzersekt is estate-grown grower fizz and must be bottle-fermented by the traditional method, with at least nine months on the lees. Much inexpensive Sekt is instead tank made from base wine bought in from elsewhere in Europe.

q: Outside Champagne, which word on a French label guarantees the wine was made by the traditional method?
exp: Cremant d'Alsace, de Bourgogne, de Loire and the rest share rules on hand harvesting, whole-bunch pressing and a minimum time on the lees.

q: Which country turned a sparkling red made from Shiraz into a national specialty?
exp: Usually off dry, soft in tannin and served lightly chilled. It is a fixture of an Australian Christmas table, where the holiday falls in high summer.

q: South African bottle-fermented sparkling wine is sold under which designation?
exp: The first South African bottle-fermented sparkler was made in 1971, but the Cap Classique name dates from 1992, adopted once the Champagne terms were closed off. Chardonnay and Pinot Noir lead the blends, with Chenin Blanc still widely used.

q: Served cool alongside the cured pork and Parmigiano of Emilia, which frothy red is the local staple?
exp: Lambrusco is a family of related varieties grown around Modena and Reggio. The good bottles are dry and tank made, and their acidity and light tannin cut straight through fat.

q: Grape spirit goes into Port partway through fermentation. What does that achieve?
opts: It strips colour out of the must
It stops the ferment and leaves sugar
It removes sugar and raises the acidity
exp: Fermentation is stopped at around six or seven percent alcohol and the spirit takes the wine close to twenty. The sweetness is grape sugar the yeast never reached.

q: Port's vineyards climb the terraced schist of which river valley?
exp: A hot, dry valley sheltered from Atlantic weather by the Serra do Marao. The wine takes its name from Oporto at the river mouth, though the shippers built their ageing lodges across the water in Vila Nova de Gaia.

q: Of the Douro's red varieties, which is generally rated the finest for Port?
exp: Touriga Franca, Tinta Roriz, Tinta Barroca and Tinto Cao complete the classic five. Blending is the norm, and old vineyards are often planted as a field mixture.

q: Bottled after about two years in wood and then left to mature for decades in glass, this style is declared only in exceptional years. Which is it?
exp: A declaration is the shipper's own judgement and comes perhaps three times a decade. The wine goes into bottle unfiltered, throws a heavy crust, and must be decanted.

q: A pale amber rim and flavours of walnut and dried fig in a Port point to what?
opts: Fermentation under a veil of yeast
Long ageing in bottle after two years in wood
A short maceration and very early bottling
Long ageing in cask before bottling
exp: Air reaching the wine through the wood browns it and builds nutty, dried-fruit flavour. The permitted age indications are ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty and eighty years, and each states the style a tasting panel judges the blend to show rather than a verified average.

q: A wood-aged Port from one named harvest, kept in cask for at least seven years, is sold as what?
exp: A Colheita carries a year like a vintage Port but has done its ageing in cask, so it needs no decanting. The label gives the bottling date as well as the harvest.

q: Four to six years in cask, then bottled ready to drink: which Port designation is that?
exp: LBV comes from a single year but does its formative ageing in wood rather than glass. Most is filtered and pours clear; unfiltered bottlings still throw a deposit.
